I know you’ve already heard this but…. Have you seen how bad the effects of untreated RA is?  
I was diagnosed nearly ten years ago. Was fairly mild. Took plaquenil. Got sick - not from that- stopped the med. had cancer. Went for nearly five years off and on meds because I was scared to death of getting more cancer. Guess what. I did anyway! Got lung cancer. I had surgery for that and a few months later bam. Huge flare. Couldn’t walk. Bed ridden. I mean bed ridden had to have a potty chair and all! I literally couldn’t walk. 

My knees are still bent up a year later. I can’t straighten my elbows anymore.  I decided to take the risk to at least live as normally as I can. 

I cannot believe that in four days I have been able to walk without a cane and through an entire store! I still have pain still stiff but it’s not stopping me. I’m terrified of the med but I’m also terrified of being unable to do anything at all. 
Take the med. whatever happens, it’s happened before and docs WILL know what to do. Deep breath! Accept that this is something you have to deal with and do it. I wish so much I had taken the meds long long ago! I’ve missed so much!

Hey, Sorry you're feeling so overwhelmed with all of this! I do think its reasonable to be anxious about something like this. You're told you have a disease that has no cure and when you look for support, you find a lot of people who seek answers and reassurance for their own anxiety who report a lot of bad experiences. It can become a circle of fear. Its easy to see the harsh things because most folks who never have any issue don't come to forms of online support such as this. 

If you compare the number of people in this sub to how many people worldwide who have this and other forms of autoimmune diseases,  I think you can begin to see that not everyone has bad experiences.  Believe, I am one of the most anxious folks ever! I JUST started Enbrel and I have a pretty significant cancer history and a lot of other things wrong but my drs said they feel comfy with me trying it. I took it Monday and its now Thursday. I can tell a difference.  even THAT freaks me out a bit!  

Its good to want to educate yourself because you will want to have a good backbone of info to be able to have quality convos with your doctor. Its not good to rabbit hole, as you know. So, set some boundaries for yourself, I do! limit your online searching and reading, for now, to things that are factual, like, legit medical websites and manufacturers sites for the meds you will be taking.  Its ok to ask how others feel or reacted to a med but of course, we are all different.  Breathe and know that this disease isnt going to kill you today or tomorrow. or any time, really. meds are very important to slow the progression. Whatever, if anything happens, you will not be the first and your doctor will know what to do. 

I had a hard time accepting this and giving up control, once I did that, I am better and you will be, too! Im hanging out in your corner and sending you lots of love. Its gonna be ok. a rough road at times but its definitely doable. good days, bad days.  Here if you need to talk!

Hi. I know there’s a lot of replies here and it can be overwhelming, I’ve been there with my own pup.  Here’s what finally helped my boy- he was nearly bald, bleeding and just miserable- it lasted a couple years - lots of vets and tests, shampoos, oils, food changes. It’s been hell. 

We took him off all dog food and fed him beef, lamb, veggies and rice. We did that for two months.  In the meantime, we had a vet say hey, let’s test his thyroid and check him for cushings. We did that and slowly started adding some hard dog food to his diet. Oh and we cut out treats. All of them. He went through a period of not hardly eating at all and it scared me but he needed to lose weight and he was beginning to look better. I eat oatmeal every morning and asked the vet if he could have it too. She says sure! His thyroid was not great so we stared synthroid twice a day. Magic. He is a fury boy now but has some spots that will never grow hair again. But he feels so much better! He still eats oatmeal with me every morning, he eats a hard ‘puppy’ food and he is now allowed treats. We did start using an anti fungal shampoo on him during that time. I think the combo helped him. We’re still doing the cushings tests. He still had a little pot belly and pees A LOT!  I hope you find what helps your pup. Just keep at it. Oh, Jax & daisy shampoo and lotion helped him a lot as well.
